title: The residual /trim gates
description: The two /trim gates no extractor answers, plus the two clauses left behind by the four that became a facts verb. Every question below is lifted from the Rubric section of src/commands/trim.md; none is invented here.
actsNote: Nothing acts on an answer from this set. Nothing-acting is the safety mechanism, not shadow mode. See docs/adrs/0008-no-question-set-acts-in-this-campaign.md.
batchNote: The four nouls below go out in ONE call, per the Speculative Fan-Out pattern. They share a state and are independent of each other's answers.

excluded.reason: Four of /trim's six gates are computable from the transcript machinery the hooks already run, so they are answered by a my-command-tools facts verb and never sent to the classifier. Routing a deterministic boolean through a probabilistic classifier adds a network round trip, a confidence band, and a failure mode to a computation that has none.

gates.half: the returned-calls half — the last turn's calls all returned, none came back is_error, and no Monitor or backgrounded call is still live
in full — turns since the last compaction boundary carrying a call that is not read-only, plus hasWork and diffStat from state
the arithmetic half — the repeat-identical-probe and repeat-error counts the existing gates already derive
in full — an unreturned Agent dispatch, a live watch, or an unmerged path from git diff --diff-filter=U

state.note: Prose, deliberately. Every question in this set is unanswerable from a shape-only digest, and a payload that cannot answer its own questions is worse than no payload. The precis is conversation-derived state that leaves the device: gated twice, off by default, and printable in full with --dry-run before anything is sent.

eval.statement: THIS SET CARRIES NO EVAL NUMBERS. Do not look for one elsewhere; none exists. /trim's six gates are answered inside a live conversation and the verdict is written nowhere — no commit, no artifact, no verdict.json field — so there is no recorded ground truth to measure agreement against. A corpus may accrue later, prospectively, from shadow records paired with what the session did next.

questions.noul: The latest unit of work is complete: nothing is mid-edit, mid-command, mid-tool sequence, mid-merge resolution, or awaiting a result.
questions.answerMeans: 1.0 means the work is closed; 0.0 means it is mid-sequence.
questions.why: Every call returning cleanly is compatible with being halfway through a sequence the agent intends to finish, so the extractor's returned-calls half cannot answer this clause.

questions.noul: A replacement summary can preserve the original goal and acceptance criteria, user decisions and constraints, branch/worktree and dirty state, files changed and why, commands and tests run with their outcomes, confirmed findings, relevant failed approaches, unresolved risks or blockers, and the exact next action.
questions.answerMeans: 1.0 means a replacement summary preserves all of it; 0.0 means compaction would lose something on that list.
questions.why: No extractor reads a summary that does not exist yet and judges what it would preserve.

questions.noul: Recent work is cycling or repeatedly failing such that compressing it would hide useful negative evidence or make the same attempts likely.
questions.answerMeans: 1.0 means compressing would hide evidence worth keeping; 0.0 means it would not. This gate is safe when the answer is low.
questions.why: The repeat count is arithmetic and the worth of the evidence is not.

questions.noul: Any work currently treated as complete has received the relevant verification. Answer low when verification is still required or its result is unknown.
questions.answerMeans: 1.0 means everything treated as done was verified; 0.0 means verification is outstanding or its result is unknown.
questions.why: Whether a given verification was the relevant one for a given piece of work is a comparison no extractor makes.
